Which TWO points do Thomas and Jeanne make about Thomas's sporting activities at school?

Questions 23 and 24

Choose TWO letters, A-E.

Which TWO feelings did Thomas experience when he was in Kenya?

Questions 25–30

Comments about the development of the equipment
A It could cause excessive sweating.
B The material was being mass produced for another purpose.
C People often needed to make their own.
D It often had to be replaced.
E The material was expensive.
F It was unpopular among spectators.

transcript.en: Hi Thomas, how are you enjoying the course so far?
transcript.zh: 嗨，Thomas，到目前为止你对这门课感觉如何？

transcript.en: Yeah, I think it’s good.
transcript.zh: 嗯，我觉得很好。

transcript.en: Remind me - why did you decide to study sports science? Didn't you want to be a professional athlete when you were at school?
transcript.zh: 我忽然想起来——为什么你决定学习体育科学？你上学的时候不是想成为一名职业运动员吗？

transcript.en: Yeah -that was my goal, and all my classmates assumed I would achieve it; theythought I was brilliant.
transcript.zh: 是的，这是我的目标，并且我所有的同学都认为我会成功；他们认为我很有天赋。

transcript.en: That must have been a nice feeling.
transcript.zh: 那一定感觉很棒吧。

transcript.en: Mm, I thought I could win anything. There was no one who could run faster  than me.
transcript.zh: 嗯，我以为我能赢得任何比赛。没有人能跑得比我快。

transcript.en: Exactly - so what happened? Did your mum and dad want you to be more ‘academic’?
transcript.zh: 没错，所以究竟发生了什么？你爸妈想让你更“追求学业”吗？

transcript.en: Not at all. Perhaps they should have pushed me harder, though.
transcript.zh: 完全不是的。不过，也许他们应该敦促我让我更加努力。

transcript.en: What do you mean?
transcript.zh: 什么意思？

transcript.en: I think I should have practised more.
transcript.zh: 我想我应该再多加练习的。

transcript.en: What makes you say that?
transcript.zh: 你为什么会这么说？

transcript.en: Well, I went out to Kenya for a couple of weeks to train
transcript.zh: 嗯，我去肯尼亚训练了几个星期…

transcript.en: Really! I didn't know that.
transcript.zh: 真的吗？我都不知道这件事。

transcript.en: I was chosen to go there out of loads of kids and run with some of the top  teenage athletes in the world. And... I was so calm about it.
transcript.zh: 我是在众多孩子中被选中去那里的，与世界上一些顶尖的青少年运动员一起跑步。而且…我对此很平静。

transcript.en: I just kept thinking how fortunate I was. What a great chance this was! Everyone back home was so proud of me.
transcript.zh: 我只是一直在想我是多么的幸运。这是多么好的机会啊！家里的每个人都为我感到骄傲。

transcript.en: But once we started competing, I very quickly realised I wasn‘t good enough
transcript.zh: 但是一旦当我们开始比赛时，我很快就意识到我还不够优秀。

transcript.en: That must have been a huge shock.
transcript.zh: 那一定是一个巨大的打击。

transcript.en: I thought  'this can't be happening'! I was used to winning.
transcript.zh: 我觉得‘这不可能啊’！我已经习惯赢了。

transcript.en: I'm sorry to hear that.
transcript.zh: 听到这个消息我很难过。

transcript.en: It's OK. I'm over it now and I think it’s much better to do a university course and  this one has such a variety of sports-related areas.
transcript.zh: 没关系的。我现在已经适应了，我认为学习大学课程要更好一些，这门课程有很多与体育相关的领域。

transcript.en: It's going to be good.
transcript.zh: 一定会很棒的。

transcript.en: Oh, I agree–I chose it because of that.
transcript.zh: 哦，我同意——我选择它就是出于这个原因。

transcript.en: So Jeanne-have you thought of any ideas for the discussion session next week on technology and sport?
transcript.zh: 那么Jeanne下周关于科技和体育主题的讨论会你有什么想法吗？

transcript.en: We have to cover more than one sport, don't we?
transcript.zh: 我们必须涵盖不止一项运动，是不是？

transcript.en: Yeah.
transcript.zh: 是的。

transcript.en: You know - we always think technology is about the future,but we could gather  some ideas about past developments in sport.
transcript.zh: 你知道的，我们一直认为技术关乎未来但我们可以收集一些过去的体育发展的想法。

transcript.en: Look at early types of equipment perhaps?Uh, I remember reading something about table tennis bats once
transcript.zh: 或许可以研究一下早期不同类型的运动装备？嗯，我记得我曾经读到过一些关于乒乓球拍的资料

transcript.en: -how they  ended up being covered with pimpled rubber.
transcript.zh: 它们最终为何布满了橡胶颗粒。

transcript.en: Cos they were just wooden at first, I'd imagine.
transcript.zh: 因为我想，一开始它们只是木头拍子而已。

transcript.en: Yeah. In about the 1920s, a factory was making rolls of the rubber in bulk for something like horse harnesses.
transcript.zh: 是的。大约在20世纪20年代，一家工厂正在批量生产橡胶卷，用于马具之类的东西。

transcript.en: Really!
transcript.zh: 真的吗？

transcript.en: Yeah -and someone realised that it’d make a perfect covering for the wooden bats.
transcript.zh: 是的——然后有人意识到这是可以用于木制球拍的完美的一层覆盖物。

transcript.en: So what about cricket - that’s had a few innovative changes.  Maybe the pads they wear on their legs?
transcript.zh: 板球怎么样——它已经经历了一些创新的变化。或许可以考虑一下运动员们腿上戴的护具？

transcript.en: I don't think they've changed much but, I’m just looking on the internet ...and it  says that when the first cricket helmet came in, in 1978,
transcript.zh: 我认为他们没有很大改变，但是，我只是在互联网上看到的 网络上说当第一个板球头盔在1978年出现时

transcript.en: the Australian batsman who first wore it was booed and jeered by people watching because it was so  ugly!
transcript.zh: 第一次戴它的澳大利亚击球手被观众嘘和嘲笑，因为它太丑了！

transcript.en: Wow, players have to protect themselves from getting hurt! I mean everyone wears one now.
transcript.zh: 哇，运动员必须要保护自己不受伤害！现在每名运动员都戴着头盔。

transcript.en: Mm, unlike the cycle helmet.
transcript.zh: 嗯，这和自行车头盔不一样。

transcript.en: Well, unless you're a professional but you're right, many ordinary bikers don't  wear a helmet.
transcript.zh: 嗯，除非你是职业选手不过你是对的，很多普通骑车的人都不戴头盔。

transcript.en: Hey, look at these pictures of original helmet designs. This one looks like an upside-down bowl!
transcript.zh: 嘿，看看这些原始头盔设计的照片。这个看起来像一个倒置的碗！

transcript.en: Yet, the woman's laughing-she's so proud to be wearing it!
transcript.zh: 然而，这位女士在笑她为自己戴着它而骄傲！

transcript.en: It says serious cyclists ended up with wet hair from all the hard exercise.
transcript.zh: 上面说，认真的自行车运动员最终会因为艰苦训练而湿了头发。

transcript.en: I guess that's why they have large air vents in them now so that the skin can  breathe more easily.
transcript.zh: 我猜这就是为什么他们现在有很大的气孔，这样皮肤可以更容易呼吸。

transcript.en: OK, so we've done helmets What about golf balls or better still golf clubs–they’ve changed a lot.
transcript.zh: 好了，关于头盔的部分我们已经完成了。下面看看高尔夫球或者高尔夫球杆怎么样——它们变化很大。

transcript.en: Yeah - I remember my great grandfather telling me that because a club was made entirely of wood,it would easily break and players had to get another.
transcript.zh: 是的——我记得我的曾祖父告诉我，因为球杆完全由木头制成 所以很容易断裂，球员们不得不另找一根。

transcript.en: There's no wood at all in them now, is there?
transcript.zh: 现在球杆材质一点木头都没有了，是吗？

transcript.en: No -they’re much more powerful.
transcript.zh: 没有了，他们变得更强有力了。

transcript.en: The same must be true of hockey sticks.
transcript.zh: 曲棍球棒肯定也是如此。

transcript.en: I don't think so because players still use wooden sticks today. What it does say here, though, is that when the game started you had to produce a stick yourself.
transcript.zh: 我并不这么认为，因为运动员直到今天还在用木棍。不过，这里说的是 当游戏开始时，你必须自己制作一根球棍。

transcript.en: I guess they just weren't being manufactured. So, one more perhaps. What about football?
transcript.zh: 我猜他们只是没有被批量生产出来。所以，再换一项运动。足球怎么样？

transcript.en: Well, I know the first balls were made of animal skin.
transcript.zh: 嗯，我知道第一个球是用兽皮做的。

transcript.en: Yeah, they covered them with pieces of leather that were stitched together, but the balls let in water when it rained.
transcript.zh: 是的，他们用缝合在一起的皮革覆盖在表面，但是下雨的时候球会进水。

transcript.en: Oh, that would have made them much heavier.
transcript.zh: 哦，那会使它们更重。

transcript.en: That's right. You can imagine the damage to players' necks when the ball was headed.
transcript.zh: 没错。你可以想象当球飞过来的时候，球员的脖子会受到怎样的伤害。

transcript.en: How painful that must have been!
transcript.zh: 那一定会很痛！

transcript.en: Yeah, well, I think we can put together some useful ideas
transcript.zh: 是的，嗯，我想我们可以汇总一些有价值的想法…
